paragraphs: Coach Matt opened the old cupboard on the school field. Sports day was on Friday, and he had a new game for the class. "What's this?" he asked, and he held up a tennis racket. "It's a tennis racket," said Lily. "And this is a skateboard," said Sam. "You like skateboarding," said Ben. At the back, there were ice skates and roller skates. Everyone looked at the skates. "What does roller skating mean?" asked Ben. "It means skating with wheels," said Coach Matt. "Ice skating is for cold places." "Roller skating is our new game!"

Tom put on the roller skates, and Coach Matt held his arm. Tom skated badly at first. Sam and Lily watched from the grass. Tom's arms went out, and he fell down two times. "Move your shoulders," said Coach Matt. "Look in front of you." Tom practiced again and again. Then Tom did not fall. "I did it!" he shouted. "Yes, you did!" said Lily.

The sun was hot, and the field was full of children. Then the children made two teams for a race. Tom was in the red team, and Ben was in the blue team. Ben skated faster than Tom. Tom went more slowly, but he went more carefully. Did Tom win the race? No, he didn't. But he didn't fall! Everyone clapped, and Coach Matt gave Tom a big smile. "That was exciting!" said Tom. "I like roller skating!"
